problem.concept: existing models generate one representation per word and do not consider different meanings of a word

task.concept: learn multiple topic-sensitive representations per word

method.concept: integrating topic distributions for each document

contribution.concept: two approaches to learn multiple topic-sensitive representations per word
modeling topics and integrating topic distributions for each document we obtain representations that are able to distinguish between different meanings of a given word

Our models yield statistically significant improvements for the lexical substitution task indicating that commonly used single word representations, even when combined with contextual information, are insufficient for this task

review_notes: Added the explicitly evaluated lexical substitution setting to task; checked the single-representation limitation, HDP and separate topic procedures, and the contextual-information caveat.

problem.concept: previous work has largely used independent classifiers

contribution.concept: joint model of argument frames
system achieves an error reduction of 22% on all arguments and 32% on core arguments over a state-of-the art independent classifier for gold-standard parse trees on PropBank

review_notes: Checked all four source sentences: joint argument-frame model and interaction features are distinct from log-linear modeling; retained PropBank and the 22%/32% results with gold-standard parse-tree condition. No semantic correction needed.

problem.concept: Abstract-like text summarisation requires a means of producing novel summary sentences

contribution.concept: new search algorithm for this task that models argument satisfaction
Using BLEU to measure performance on a string regeneration task, we found an improvement, illustrating the benefit of the spanning tree approach armed with an argument satisfaction model

review_notes: Added the explicit string regeneration evaluation setting to task; checked the global dependency structure, argument satisfaction, bipartite matching and BLEU-qualified improvement.

contribution.concept: survey on the role of negation in sentiment analysis

small corpus of 5,139 sentences with propositional opinion information

review_notes: A3 ends mid-phrase after "associating them with propositional". Removed the shortened extension finding because its complete relation target is unavailable; preserved the intact parser extension and annotated-corpus artifacts for audit only.

Source is an expository Monte Carlo definition rather than a reported research study, and A2 contains a visibly broken piecewise distribution formula. Empty research facets retained; exclude whole paper from the usable teacher pool.

problem.concept: whether preferential attachment occurs during the growth of a network

task.concept: determine whether preferential attachment occurs during the growth of a network
extract the preferential attachment rule using time-dependent data

method.concept: examine the growth of the network as a function of a threshold energy (rather than time)

contribution.concept: self-consistent method
method, which is seen to be robust

Even though this network is static, we can examine the growth of the network as a function of a threshold energy (rather than time), where only those transition states with energies lower than the threshold energy contribute to the network.For these networks we are able to detect the presence of preferential attachment, and this helps to explain the ubiquity of funnels on energy landscapes.

scale-free degree distribution shows some differences from that of a model network grown using the obtained preferential attachment rules, implying that other factors are also important in the growth process

review_notes: Added threshold-energy growth analysis as a distinct procedure; expanded the preferential-attachment finding to retain the static-network setting and lower-than-threshold transition-state restriction. Retained the separate mismatch/counter-factor finding.

problem.concept: mathematical implication of the Rasch model should be studied further in order to understand how and why it conflicts with the joining assumption

task.concept: pursues the mathematics of the Rasch model

method.concept: special case when the sizes of the categories are equal

contribution.concept: This paper pursues the mathematics of the Rasch model and establishes, through a special case when the sizes of the categories are equal and when the model is expressed in the multiplicative metric, that its probability distribution reflects the precision with which the data are collected, and that if a pair of categories is collapsed after the data are collected, it no longer reflects the original precision.
As a consequence, and not because of a qualitative change in the variable, the joining assumption is destroyed when categories are combined

review_notes: Replaced the topical nondichotomization task with the actual mathematical analysis; added multiplicative metric. Restored the paper as the claimant and the equal-category/multiplicative-metric assumptions to the original-versus-collapsed precision result. Minor joined-word typography does not remove the intact A6/A7 claims.
